simple.meaning: אָשֵׁם (ʼâshêm) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “guilty ; hence, presenting a sin-offering.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 3 times across Genesis, 2 Samuel, Ezra, beginning at Genesis 42:21. Its contexts include family, flock, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אָשֵׁם (H818).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: אָשֵׁם (ʼâshêm) / H818 is traced through Genesis 42:21, 2 Samuel 14:13, Ezra 10:19 as a generated source-based concept entry.

firstOccurrence.englishText: They said to one another, “We are certainly guilty concerning our brother, in that we saw the distress of his soul, when he begged us, and we wouldn’t listen. Therefore this distress has come upon us.”

majorEvents.label: Offering
majorEvents.evidenceText: They gave their hand that they would put away their wives; and being guilty, they offered a ram of the flock for their guilt.

timeline.evidenceText: They said to one another, “We are certainly guilty concerning our brother, in that we saw the distress of his soul, when he begged us, and we wouldn’t listen. Therefore this distress has come upon us.”

The woman said, “Why then have you devised such a thing against the people of God? For in speaking this word the king is as one who is guilty, in that the king does not bring home again his banished one.
They gave their hand that they would put away their wives; and being guilty, they offered a ram of the flock for their guilt.
